newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castor ends up but off day's high.
newsitem.headline: Indian castor ends up but off day's high.

text.p: Indian castorseed June delivery ended Wednesday at 1,122/1,123 rupees per quintal, off the day's high of 1,133/1,135 but up from Tuuesday's closing 1,112/1,113, traders said.
"Prices went up initially on short-covering by bears but dropped on profit-taking following reports of fresh arrivals," one trader said.
Arrivals of castorseed in the eastern Indian region of Gujarat were higher today at 45,000/50,000 bags (75 kg each).
The Bombay Oil Exchange officially opened castorseed September delivery but no trade had yet taken place, traders said.
"Some of the brokers are asking for a premium of 60/70 per quintal for the September delivery against June delivery," a trader said.
Groundnut oil dropped to 358/359 rupees per 10 kg from 362/363 rupees on increased summer crop arrivals, traders said.
They said stockists were active sellers on expectation of higher arrivals of imported palm-oil and imported sunflower oil at the Bombay port in the short term.
Imported palm-oil fell to 284/285 rupees per 10 kg from 290 rupees.
In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil fell 5 rupees at 555 rupees per 15 kg.
The Bombay Oil and Oilseed (ready and forward) market is closed on Thursday for a local holiday. It reopens for trading on Friday.
